name: Joram (son of Jehoshaphat)
title: Apostate King Judah
summary: Joram was king of Judah and son of the godly king Jehoshaphat. Despite his father's example, Joram followed in the footsteps of Israel's wicked kings, influenced by his wife Athaliah, who was the daughter of Ahab. His reign was marked by idol worship, bloodshed, and military defeats.

keyEvents.title: Joram Becomes King and Kills His Brothers
keyEvents.description: When Joram took the throne, he killed all his brothers and several of Israel's leaders with the sword to secure his power.

keyEvents.title: Followed Ahab's Evil Way
keyEvents.description: Joram walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, because he married Ahab's daughter. He did what was evil in the Lord's sight.

keyEvents.title: Edom Revolts
keyEvents.description: In Joram's days, Edom broke away from Judah and set up its own king. Joram tried to defeat them but failed, and Edom has been independent ever since.

keyEvents.title: The Prophet Elijah's Letter
keyEvents.description: The prophet Elijah sent a letter to Joram with judgment from the Lord because of his wickedness, idolatry, and the murder of his brothers. The letter predicted a terrible disease.

keyEvents.title: Attack by the Philistines and Arabs
keyEvents.description: The Lord stirred up the anger of the Philistines and Arabs against Joram. They attacked Judah, broke into the land, and took everything they found in the king's house, including his sons and wives.

keyEvents.title: Joram's Illness and Death
keyEvents.description: The Lord struck Joram with an incurable disease in his intestines. After two years of suffering, he died, and no one mourned for him. He was not buried in the royal tombs.
